query: W melts near 3422 °C, whereas Cu boils near 2562 °C, so conventional induction or arc-plasma casting cannot readily yield a uniform W–Cu material. Phase separation and void formation can impair thermal transport. Filling a W skeleton with molten Cu or Cu powder can leave defects; spark-plasma sintering and mechanical alloying can produce finer, more uniform structures but can also leave voids; vapor-coated W powders have been sintered to achieve near-perfect contact between the constituents; and metal 3D printing has also been explored. Starting from W particles or connected W regions within a Cu matrix for heat transfer under irradiation in fusion-reactor joints, what single intervention could overcome these limitations while preserving mechanical durability? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention and mechanism, predicts an outcome relative to a named existing fabrication baseline, defines the processing and service boundaries, cites supporting prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment and observations that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Room-temperature galvanostatic electrodeposition of Cu into a 3D-printed W foam skeleton produces a conformal, epitaxial Cu coating that eliminates interfacial voids and increases overall thermal conductivity by at least 10% compared to spark-plasma-sintered W–Cu composites while retaining mechanical durability under fusion-joint conditions.
generation.material_initial_state: 3D-printed W foam skeleton (60% porosity, strut diameter ≈200 µm)
generation.intervention: Room-temperature galvanostatic Cu electrodeposition at 50 mA/cm² from a CuSO₄ bath to fully infiltrate and coat the W foam
generation.conditions: Processing: 25 °C, 50 mA/cm², 2 h deposition on W foam with strut diameters 100–500 µm; Service: temperatures up to 400 °C and neutron irradiation up to 1 dpa
generation.structural_mediator: Conformal, epitaxial Cu layer bridging W struts to eliminate interfacial voids
generation.mechanism: Electrochemical nucleation and growth of Cu on W yields full wetting and intimate contact, reducing thermal boundary resistance without high-temperature sintering
generation.predicted_outcome: Composite thermal conductivity ≥330 W/m·K (≥10% above spark-plasma-sintered baseline) with interfacial void fraction <1% and mechanical strength within 10% of baseline
generation.baseline: Spark-plasma-sintered W–Cu composite (50 vol% W) with thermal conductivity ~300 W/m·K
generation.boundary: Processing variables: W strut diameter 100–500 µm; current density 25–100 mA/cm²; Service: T≤400 °C, irradiation ≤1 dpa
generation.uncertainty: Moderate, due to limited data on irradiation-induced interface stability at <1 dpa

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate W foam–Cu composites by (a) spark plasma sintering of W and Cu powders and (b) proposed electrodeposition into identical W foams. Compare thermal and mechanical properties.
measurements: bulk thermal conductivity (laser flash or guarded hot plate)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If electrodeposited composites exhibit thermal conductivity ≤305 W/m·K, interfacial void fraction ≥2%, or mechanical strength drop >10% relative to SPS baseline, the hypothesis is falsified.
